inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q1 FY2027 diluted weighted average 404.290M (8-K ex99, 2026-09-23); 399.517M basic outstanding at 2026-08-31 plus ~4.8M dilutive options. Held FLAT because SBC plus equity-award withholding taxes are fully expensed in the flows. Standalone count: excludes ~14.4M CTAS shares issuable to UniFirst holders (0.7720 x ~18.6M UNF shares) if the pending merger closes.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation $128.076M + shares acquired for employee-partner payroll taxes $174.319M (XBRL AdjustmentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation). No combined company figure is published (Cintas reports no adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation), so the two lines are summed. 3-yr average of the combined charge is 3.2% of revenue (FY24 3.1%, FY25 3.7%, FY26 2.7%).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), beta ~1.0 (defensive B2B route-based services, but employment-sensitive), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~9.3%. Debt is ~3% of EV (US$2.43bn vs ~US$81bn market cap) at ~4% pre-tax -> WACC ~9.1% on market weights; 8.5% used for a 50-year record of through-cycle compounding with low revenue volatility (worst year FY2010, -6%). Same WACC in all scenarios: risk charged once, in the scenario paths.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: lease cost ($101.2M FY2026) is already inside operating expense and hence inside EBITDA; lease liabilities ($282.5M) are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: Cintas is a US operating company (uniform rental/facility services 76% of revenue, first aid & safety 13%, fire protection & other 11%) with conventional FCF; no bank/REIT/holdco characteristics, no dual currency, SBC is material (US market) so house and street bases diverge. No memory entry existed (first valuation). EBITDA margin driver is PRE-SBC: FY2026 GAAP operating income $2,606.5M + D&A $512.8M + SBC $128.1M + UniFirst transaction costs $15.1M = $3,262.5M = 29.0% of revenue; the engine then deducts SBC+withholding taxes via sbc_pct_path. D&A includes ~1.7% of revenue of intangible and capitalized-contract-cost amortization; commission cash is captured in the working-capital drag. Working capital: FY2024-26 cash WC absorbed ~29% of each revenue-dollar of growth (rental items in service, receivables, capitalized contract costs; FY26 -46%); wc_capture -35% used. Interest income ($5.1M FY2026) not stripped: net debt, not net cash. Buybacks: $952.1M FY2026 total repurchases of which $174.3M were withholding taxes (already in the SBC charge) and $777.8M open-market; the flat count is being funded (diluted count fell 413.5M FY24 -> 404.3M Q1 FY27). UNIFIRST: merger agreed 2026-03-10 ($155 cash + 0.7720 CTAS shares per UNF share, ~US$5.5bn), UNF holders approved 2026-06-12, FTC review ongoing, close expected before end CY2026, $350M reverse termination fee. Valued STANDALONE, matching management's standalone FY2027 guidance; at a fair price the deal is value-neutral before synergies, so the standalone value is the right anchor and synergies are an upside not in any scenario. Revisit on close: add issued shares, deal debt and UNF flows together.
inputs.dividend_note: Quarterly dividend US$208.8M paid 2026-09-15; dividends are a use of owner FCF, not a deduction from it.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.9% diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR 13.3%: book value is depressed by US$0.7-1.5bn/yr of buybacks plus a rising dividend, so equity CAGR understates the compounding. Revenue CAGR (FY21-26 9.6%, incl. ~1-2pp tuck-in M&A) is the growth anchor, as for Visa.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes): FY21 1,030.8; FY22 1,066.5; FY23 970.9; FY24 1,357.4; FY25 1,373.2; FY26 1,578.8 (US$M). 5yr owner CAGR 8.9% vs reported 9.1% - withholding taxes grew faster than FCF (74.5 -> 174.3, peak 255.5 in FY25) as a rising share price inflated the tax on option exercises. The 3yr figures start from an FY23 trough (capex and inventory build), so 17.6% overstates the run rate. EPS is diluted and split-adjusted (4:1 split Sep-2024).

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = midpoint of raised FY2027 standalone guidance US$12.15-12.27bn (+7.9-8.9%, one extra workday); Q1 FY27 organic +8.9%. Decelerates 0.5pp/yr toward terminal as penetration of the ~16m uncovered US workers and first-aid/fire cross-sell matures.
base.margin_rationale: FY26 pre-SBC EBITDA margin 29.0%; Q1 FY27 operating margin 24.1% ex-deal costs (+140bp y/y). Operating margin has expanded ~75bp/yr FY22-26 (20.2% -> 23.3%); base halves that pace and plateaus near 31.8%.

scenario_narratives.base: Cintas keeps compounding as the route-density leader in US uniform rental and facility services: FY2027 lands at the midpoint of raised standalone guidance (+8.4%), then growth fades 0.5pp a year to 4% as new-customer wins from the no-programme segment and first-aid/fire cross-sell mature. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin rises from 29.0% to ~31.8% on SmartTruck routing, the SAP/technology programme and procurement scale, at roughly half the FY22-26 pace of expansion. Cash taxes stay near the guided ~20.5-21% and working capital keeps absorbing ~35c of every incremental revenue dollar (garments in service, receivables, capitalised commissions).
scenario_narratives.bull: Cintas sustains high-single-digit organic growth for five-plus years - uniform penetration of the uncovered workforce, first aid and fire protection growing low-teens, pricing holding above cost inflation - and operating leverage from route density plus technology lifts pre-SBC EBITDA margin to ~33.5%, in line with the trajectory of FY22-26. No recession interrupts the path. UniFirst synergies are NOT included even here; they would be additive.
scenario_narratives.bear: A US employment downturn hits the core axis - uniform wearers are headcount - as it did in FY2010 (revenue -6%): growth collapses to ~2% in year two, energy, cotton and labour costs squeeze margin back to ~28% and it only recovers to 29%. Separately, UniFirst integration distracts management or the FTC blocks the deal (US$350M reverse fee, not in the flows), and long-run growth settles at 3% as the market saturates. The business stays highly cash generative - there is no solvency risk at <1x net debt/EBITDA.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (up from the 15% default): the business is cycle-exposed through customer headcount and the next US downturn is plausible within the horizon, plus a large pending acquisition under FTC review. Base 55%: the path is anchored on explicitly raised guidance and a long compounding record. Bull 25% (down from 35%): it needs both sustained ~9% growth and continued ~70bp/yr margin expansion without a recession for five years - two independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cintas is one of the highest-quality compounders in US services, and the model grants it that: 8% near-term growth, continued margin expansion and a Gordon-bound terminal at 8.5%/3%. The valuation still sits well below the price because the market (~40x trailing earnings, ~50x trailing owner FCF) is capitalising the FY22-26 margin-expansion rate into perpetuity. House basis charges SBC plus the cash withholding taxes on option exercises (~2.7-3.7% of revenue), which the street's 'free cash flow' treats as free.
key_risks_to_valuation: Employment-cycle exposure: revenue tracks customer headcount; FY2010 revenue fell 6%.
UniFirst merger (~US$5.5bn, ~14.4M new shares + ~US$2.9bn cash) pending FTC review; valued standalone. Synergies would lift value; a block costs a US$350M reverse fee.
Equity-award withholding taxes are volatile (US$74M FY21 -> US$255M FY25) and scale with the share price; the combined SBC charge could run above the 2.5-2.9% path.
Terminal value is ~65-70% of EV; each 1pp of WACC moves value ~20%.
Margin expansion has been the main driver of EPS compounding; a plateau below 30% pre-SBC EBITDA removes most of the base-case margin uplift.
